text:
Maya (Finance): Heads up — noticed ~120 invoices created in Stripe over the last 48h that synced into NetSuite under the wrong subsidiary. Appears to be a fuzzy-match hit during customer resolution after the email normalization change we deployed Friday.
Liam (Billing Eng): ack. I pulled some examples. Looks like our fuzzy matcher prioritized domain and dropped the tax_country token when email domain normalizes to lower-case. Some EU customers ended up on the US subsidiary.
Maya (Finance): ugh. This is causing currency and tax-code mismatches on posted invoices. We haven't closed the month yet but close is in 7 days. Need to avoid manual churn.
Liam (Billing Eng): sample mapping from logs:
```
stripe_invoice: inv_3KlaXx
stripe_customer: cus_J2a9
ns_customer_match: ns_10234 (matched by email: john@Acme.CO -> matched to acme.co/us)
expected_ns_customer: ns_55221 (acme.co/eu)
```
Liam (Billing Eng): root cause: our email normalization removed the subdomain token used by the legacy resolver, and NetSuite subsidiary selection used that token to pick EU vs US. Fuzzy threshold also bumped a tie to US.
SyncBot: 2 DLQ messages for webhook: stripe->net-sync (retention=72h) — message_ids: dlq_77a, dlq_77b
Jordan (Platform SRE): @Liam can you confirm whether DLQ entries were reprocessed automatically? If so, might have re-applied with wrong mapping.
Liam (Billing Eng): DLQ was NOT auto-reprocessed — these were ingested once and mapped at ingest-time. Backfill will be required to fix net-posts.
Sarah (Accounting): We need an approach that preserves audit trail. Prefer reversing wrong NS invoices and creating corrected ones rather than mass editing, unless there's low impact.
Maya (Finance): Agree with Sarah. We should estimate number and total value before picking approach. Also need GL impact and whether we can do a corrective journal instead.
Liam (Billing Eng): I can run a safe dry-run backfill that identifies all affected invoices and produces a proposed actions CSV. Query I'm going to run:
```
SELECT si.id as stripe_invoice, si.customer_id, ns.match_id, ns.subsidiary, si.amount
FROM stripe_invoices si
JOIN ns_matches ns ON ns.stripe_customer = si.customer_id
WHERE si.created_at > '2026-03-20' AND ns.confidence < 0.9 AND ns.subsidiary != si.expected_subsidiary;
```
Liam (Billing Eng): dry-run will be read-only. After review we can schedule corrective job that either posts reversal + reissue or updates NS via API with a note and idempotency key.
Jordan (Platform SRE): If we do programmatic corrections, we must ensure idempotency and write a changelog record (ns_change_id) so accounting can reconcile. Also recommend rate-limiting to avoid locking NetSuite.
Sarah (Accounting): Please include columns: original_ns_id, original_post_date, currency, tax_code, tax_amount, suggested_action, supporting_stripe_invoice_link.
Maya (Finance): Timeline? We need the CSV by EOD tomorrow to sign off before week-end. If it's > 400 invoices, could be a runbook with approvals.
Liam (Billing Eng): I'll start dry-run now and post the CSV in #finance-private (sensitive). Expect initial CSV within 10h. Will include estimated GL delta.
Maya (Finance): Also loop in Legal if any cross-border tax reclassification needed. @Jordan can you brief infra on throttling plan? We may hold corrective push until weekend window.
Jordan (Platform SRE): Will prepare throttled runner and alerting for failures. If approval given, aim for Sunday 03:00 UTC window.
Sarah (Accounting): :thumbsup: Approve dry-run and Sunday window tentatively. Final sign-off after CSV review.
Liam (Billing Eng): noted. I'll add a runbook step to snapshot current NetSuite invoices (export) and to tag corrected invoices with "redwood:correction:2026-03-23".
Maya (Finance): Thanks — please include rollback steps and manual-cutover checklist. High priority but want zero surprises at month close.
SyncBot: Reminder: monthly-exports job scheduled Wed 06:00 UTC — consider disabling export during correction window to avoid dupes.
Maya (Finance): Good catch. Jordan please make sure exports paused during the push.
Jordan (Platform SRE): will do. I'll also add a smoke-check that compares totals by subsidiary after the run.
Maya (Finance): OK team — proceed with dry-run. Post CSV and a short summary in this thread when ready. Thanks.
